stem: In the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG), what are the three levels of conformance used to categorize testable success criteria for the WCAG 2.2?

options.text: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA
options.shortLabel: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA
options.rationale: WCAG 2.2 organizes its testable success criteria into three conformance levels—A, AA, and AAA—where Level A represents the minimum baseline and Level AAA represents the highest level of accessibility.
WCAG 2.2 does not use numbered tiers, its testable success criteria are categorized under Levels A, AA, and AAA.
Bronze, Silver, and Gold are not WCAG conformance levels; WCAG 2.2 categorizes all testable success criteria under Levels A, AA, and AAA.
WCAG 2.2 does not classify conformance using labels such as Basic, Standard, or Full; it defines conformance through Levels A, AA, and AAA.

explanation: The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG 2) are organized under four principles (perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust) and include testable success criteria that determine conformance at three levels: Level A, Level AA, and Level AAA. Most laws and accessibility policies worldwide (including EN 301 549 and Section 508) reference Level AA as the standard conformance target.
